reads.need: A balanced town that is losing people
reads.evidence: 2,731 postings against 54,869 households: about 5 for every 100 households, a seventh of El Segundo's rate. The Census has the population down 5.8% since 2020.
reads.quality: Torrance has the homes and a broad mix of work. The open question is why residents are leaving a town with both.
reads.move: Find out who is leaving: by age, by renter or owner, by neighborhood. That decides whether the answer is housing cost, schools or something else.
reads.why: The population figure is official. The reason for the drop is not in any data we hold.

reads.need: Hands-on work is a real share here
reads.evidence: 174 technician and trades postings and 123 in nursing and care, next to 380 for engineers.
reads.quality: More of the openings are reachable without a four-year degree than in El Segundo, and more of them are the care jobs residents rely on.
reads.move: Pair the two towns. El Segundo's employers post few technician roles and Torrance posts three times as many. A shared listing of technician openings across both is a small first step.
reads.why: Same title-matching limits as everywhere on this page.

reads.evidence: A mean commute of 26.9 minutes, against 23.6 in El Segundo.
reads.quality: A little over three minutes more each way is about 27 hours a year for someone working 250 days.
reads.move: Check how many of those trips end in El Segundo, Hawthorne and the airport area, where the jobs are thickest.
reads.why: Survey averages from 2020–2024, which include the remote-work years.
